faqs.q: Birds are nesting in my Crystal City vent — which birds can be removed?
faqs.a: Only the unprotected species: European starlings, house sparrows, and pigeons are Virginia's designated nuisance birds, and those are the vent, soffit, and sign birds our crew removes and then screens out in Crystal City. faqs.q: When can bats be removed from a Rosslyn attic?
faqs.a: Bats in Virginia are handled by exclusion only — one-way exits fitted and every other opening sealed so the colony leaves on its own. Under our permit conditions the maternity season runs May 1 through August 15, and bats may not be excluded or removed then unless no young are present or there is a threat to human health or safety, so we inspect any time but schedule most Rosslyn exclusions outside that window. Since January 1, 2025, bat work also requires a CNAP holder with DWR-recognized bat training, which is how our crew works.

Shirlington.wildlife_intro:
Shirlington sits in the Four Mile Run valley, and the valley sets the call list. Fairlington's 1940s brick colonials back onto wooded stream corridor, so southern flying squirrels glide from Jennie Dean Park oaks onto slate roofs and slip in at dormer joints barely an inch wide, while striped skunks and opossums den under the low porches and garden sheds the townhome rows are full of. Down at the village center, pigeons and European starlings — two of the few birds a Virginia permit covers — nest in sign structures and loading areas.

Valley work here is patient work. Flying squirrels are colony animals, so a Shirlington job means finding every dormer and ridge gap the colony uses, fitting one-way exits, and waiting out the full departure before the last seal goes on. We close by trimming the wildlife side of the equation too — fallen fruit, unsecured pet food, and the porch voids that invite the next skunk family each spring.
